description: The Hand-in-Hand (HiH) Geospatial Platform is FAO's open-access web platform for geospatial data on food and agriculture, built as the main technical tool of FAO's Hand-in-Hand Initiative, which targets the poorest areas for agricultural investment. It provides access to millions of data layers from many domains and sources, including food security indicators and agricultural statistics, drawing on FAO flagship databases such as FAOSTAT, with data for over 245 countries and territories from 1961, and on other UN agencies, NGOs, academia, the private sector and space agencies. It is run by the FAO Agro-informatics team; linked projects include the Global Agro-Ecological Zoning version 4 and the EMPRES-i animal disease information system. Coverage is global. The platform is available online free through FAO's data applications portal, with a video tour, a quick start guide and a data catalogue with geospatial metadata; the page read states no licence for the layers. Caveats: the layers come from many providers with their own terms and dates, and the portal is a script-driven application that could not be browsed from the session. Since its launch in 2020 over 65 countries and institutions have joined its workshops. For simulation it is a single place to gather crop, land, water and food security layers as inputs to agricultural exposure, adaptation and investment models. It is related to the FAOSTAT and FAO GAEZ records in this catalogue, two of its sources.
